claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the basis of aggregate readiness passing by 2.5 points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, with the remaining developer-support API migration weakness handled through disclosure and ongoing risk management despite the mitigation runbook still being draft and unapproved.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence showed the weakness was not material for named launch use cases, certification would be more supportable.
If there were an approved mitigation or risk acceptance containing owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, the policy gap would likely be resolved.
If the final model-card disclosed the limitation before launch, certification with caveats could become compliant.
Absent one of those conditions, certification is not fully supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Evidence showing the developer-support API migration weakness is not material to any named launch use case.
An approved risk acceptance or mitigation record with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The final model-card or equivalent disclosure artifact showing whether this limitation is disclosed before launch.
Decision record tying the unresolved slice to the release policy's materiality standard.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the stated policy predicate for certification without material caveats.
The admissible record shows a current below-target developer-support migration issue concentrated in API migration guidance, so a live weakness remains.
The mitigation runbook is still draft and lacks a named approver and stop-ship threshold; under the policy text, draft monitoring does not remove the disclosure requirement.
The model-card draft says there are no known material limitations while reviewer evidence raises whether this issue should be disclosed, creating an unresolved contradiction on the record.
Public risk-management and model-card principles support monitoring and documentation, but they are not substitutes for the release policy's approval or disclosure requirements.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that current evidence shows no material weakness remains.
Any claim that the draft mitigation is sufficient to satisfy the policy requirement for an approved mitigation with required fields.
Any claim that certification is fully compliant without resolving whether the API migration guidance weakness is a material limitation for named launch use cases.
Any claim that public guidance alone supplies the missing internal policy approval or disclosure predicate.
